comparisons.peer_summary: Client operating income improved to an $897 million profit in 2024 from a $46 million operating loss in 2023, primarily due to higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD reported revenue performance recovery in their core client/computing segments in 2024, attributing growth to volume/revenue increases following prior demand weakness. Intel’s CCG revenue increased 4% due to higher notebook volume, partially offset by lower desktop demand. Similarly, AMD’s Client operating income improved significantly ($897M profit vs $46M loss) primarily due to higher revenue, though AMD also noted higher operating expenses as a counter-factor. Both disclosures highlight a recovery in consumer PC-related segments driven by volume/revenue normalization.

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discussed revenue drivers with specific mentions of 'lower demand' for certain product lines impacting overall segment performance, although the products and directions differed. Intel cited lower desktop revenue due to lower demand and exit of legacy businesses as offsets to growth. Broadcom cited lower demand for broadband and server storage products as offsets to growth in its Semiconductor Solutions segment driven by AI networking. While Intel's offset was in a legacy/PC area and Broadcom's was in enterprise infrastructure, both highlight the impact of demand softness in specific non-core or legacy buckets on the segment's net revenue.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm discussed revenue dynamics in their connectivity/mobile-facing segments involving inventory normalization. Intel's CCG revenue was driven by higher notebook volume but offset by other factors including legacy exits. Qualcomm's QCT revenue increased due to higher handset revenues, explicitly attributing part of the volume gain to 'normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year.' Both disclosures reflect a sector-wide theme of inventory normalization contributing to revenue recovery, though Intel focused on notebook volume as the primary driver and QCOM on chipset shipments.
